notes: Behavior evaluations for Work Item decomposition (SKILL.md Step 1 boundary review, validation.md AP-24/AP-25, acceptance test 19). Assertions check outcome-boundary reasoning, not domain vocabulary.

evals.target: mixed engineering types that deliver independent outcomes must split
evals.input: Evidence set: one PR adds four traceability UI views, gates Settings behind MANAGE_PROJECT capability, and migrates the icon library to Tabler 3.31.0.
assertions: Feature implementation, security/permission change, and dependency migration trigger the boundary review
They become separate Work Items because each delivers an independently meaningful outcome
The permission item states the functional access-control boundary without inventing severity or risk claims
No item merges the three merely because they share a PR/day/domain

evals.target: mixed engineering types that serve one outcome stay together
evals.input: Evidence set: commits add a domain model, an API endpoint, a UI view, and integration tests, all implementing one new Design Coverage capability.
assertions: Layer/type differences (domain vs API vs UI vs tests) do not force a split
All commits form one Work Item because they reach one shared engineering outcome
The item reports the delivered capability once, not four layer-level activities

evals.input: Evidence set: four isolated fixes (git env cleanup in specs, ts-prune exit code, E2E menu wait, smoke payload field). Draft title: 'Test infrastructure and tooling stabilization achieved'.
assertions: Acceptance test 19 flags the heading as broader than the evidence supports
The fix narrows the heading to the evidenced localized fixes (or splits items so headings match evidence)
No broad reliability/improvement claim is retained in the title or first sentence

evals.target: engineering type never forces either merge or split
evals.input: Case A: two unrelated bug fixes both in 'backend' type. Case B: a schema migration plus its data backfill plus its verification test, all different types but one outcome.
assertions: Case A splits despite matching types (independent outcomes)
Case B stays merged despite mixed types (one outcome)
Reasoning cites independent outcome, not commit, PR, domain, layer, or type labels
